summary: A clean, production-plausible Vault-like design centered on a stateless API, Postgres for strong consistency, and HSM/KMS-backed envelope encryption. The audit model (hash chains + signed WORM checkpoints) and explicit durability modes are strong, but the “everything in Postgres” choice and per-tenant hash-chain head locking look like the main scaling and operational risk at the stated event rates.
strengths: Clear consistency semantics (version pointers, leases, idempotency) with straightforward transactional implementation
Compliance-oriented audit design with tamper evidence, WORM retention, and explicit fail-closed durability options
weaknesses: Postgres as the sole control/data/audit store is a potential bottleneck (especially ~60k audit events/sec) and strict durability will amplify write pressure and tail latency
Audit hash chaining via a per-tenant/stream head update can create contention/hotspots and complicates high-throughput ingestion without careful stream sharding and batching
